# Rezva

> Wallet-agnostic payment-identifier resolution into crypto payment destinations.

## Start here

- [Wallet quickstart](/docs/for-wallets/quickstart): integrate a wallet.
- [SDKs and integration recipes](/docs/for-wallets/sdks): TypeScript-first examples and the end-to-end flow.
- [Resolver API](/docs/for-wallets/api-reference): `POST /v1/resolve`.
- [OpenAPI specification](/openapi.json): machine-readable API contract.
- [Full LLM reference](/llms-full.txt): compact implementation context for AI agents.
- [Free API and Test Merchant](/docs/dashboard/free-api): approval-free resolver testing.
- [Test wallets](/docs/reference/compatible-wallets): Mobile wallet ([mobilewallet_rezva](https://github.com/shahtab123/mobilewallet_rezva)) and Rabby Chrome clone ([rabby_chrome_rezva](https://github.com/shahtab123/rabby_chrome_rezva)).

## Core rules

- Resolve an identifier before displaying or sending a payment.
- Require `status: "active"` and `payment_ready: true`.
- Display chain, asset, token contract, network identifier, amount constraints, and destination.
- The wallet signs and broadcasts payments; Rezva does not custody funds.
- Universal Name Resolution: same `POST /v1/resolve` also resolves `.eth`, `.sol`, `.base`, and Unstoppable TLDs (API-side; no wallet client update when already calling resolve).
- External crypto names are never registered in the Identifier Registry.
- Free API keys are resolver-only and rate-limited.
- The shared Test Merchant uses one persistent identifier and destination for all developers.
- The prototype flow is: dashboard key → shared QR → `POST /v1/resolve` → Base Sepolia USDC transfer → receipt and explorer verification.
- Provider namespace, identifier, and complaint mutations require approved provider access; identifier mutations also require controller authorization.
- Dashboard Business / Users track: max 2 identifiers per controller (existing identifiers stay; new dashboard creates blocked at the limit). Wallet providers with Merchant Setup set their own per-controller limits.
